inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 1,050M basic on the 10-Q cover (2026-07-27) + ~16M RSU dilution (Q3 FY26 diluted weighted 1,069M vs ~1,053M basic). Held FLAT because SBC and equity-award withholding taxes are fully expensed in the flows (charging dilution too would double-count). QCOM is a heavy repurchaser ($8.8B FY25, $6.8B 9M FY26), so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL 10-Q Q3 FY26: ShareBasedCompensation 9M $2,579M (FY26E ~$3,450M) + PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation 9M $888M (FY26E ~$1,000M); QCOM publishes no combined figure so the two lines are summed. FY25 actual: $2,783M + $1,115M = $3,898M (8.8% of revenue).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.2 (fabless semi, handset-cycle exposure) -> cost of equity ~10.3%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (after-tax ~4.1%) on ~7% debt weight -> WACC ~9.8%, rounded to 9.5% given QTL's royalty stability. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclical and Apple/AI risk is carried in the scenario drivers and the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases immaterial relative to EV (~$1B); kept out of both flows and net debt, consistent with US GAAP opex treatment (rent sits inside EBITDA).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build (dcf-methods routing row 1/2: US fabless semiconductor + patent licensing operating company; cyclical, so mid-cycle margins and a 14x cyclical cap rather than a growth-tech 20x). First valuation of QCOM; no prior DCF. FY0 = FY2026E (fiscal year ended 2026-09-27, not yet reported): revenue = 9M actual $32,798M + Q4 guidance midpoint $10,100M ($9.7-10.5B). FY26E reported FCF ~$9.3B = 9M OCF $8,405M - capex $1,578M + Q4 est ~$2.5B; owner FCF ~$4.85B (11.3% margin) after $4.45B SBC+withholding -- depressed by a weak Q3 OCF ($991M) and AI/data-center opex build; FY25 actual owner FCF was $8,922M (20.1%). Year-1 component-built owner FCF ~$6.6B (15.6%) sits between the two. Adj EBITDA here = GAAP operating income + D&A + SBC: FY22 44.5% (peak), FY23 33.7% (trough), FY24 37.0%, FY25 37.8%, FY26E ~32.7% (9M 33.8%, Q3 28.7%). Net debt from the Q3 FY26 balance sheet: total debt $15,270M (LTD $12,781M + current LTD $1,991M + CP $498M) less cash $4,533M and current marketable securities $3,771M. Interest income (~$450M/yr) NOT stripped: QCOM is net debt, and the engine builds unlevered flows from EBITDA, so neither interest income nor expense is in the projected FCF. QSI non-marketable venture stakes (~low $bn) are excluded from the bridge (conservative). Data center AI (AI200/AI250, HUMAIN 200MW, mgmt target $5B 2027 / $15B 2029) is NOT extrapolated at face value in base: base assumes it roughly offsets Apple modem attrition; only bull gives material incremental revenue.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is unusable: book value was gutted by the FY2018 $22.6B tender/recap (equity $31B -> $0.8B) and is rebuilding from that floor, so the 5y equity CAGR (28.4%) diverges >30% from revenue (13.5%) and EPS (2.0%). EPS is distorted by the FY2018 TCJA charge and the FY2025 ~$5.7B deferred-tax charge. Owner-FCF CAGRs (25-31%) start from depressed FY2020/FY2022 working-capital troughs. Through-cycle 10y revenue CAGR (5.8%) is the honest anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes: FY20 $2,848M, FY22 $4,007M, FY23 $6,844M, FY24 $7,581M, FY25 $8,922M. Owner-FCF CAGRs run above reported because SBC+withholding grew slower than FCF over FY22-25, i.e. SBC is NOT outgrowing cash flow -- but SBC+withholding is ~9-10% of revenue, a large standing charge. Revenue 3y CAGR ~0% (FY22 peak $44.2B -> FY25 $44.3B) captures a full handset down-and-up cycle.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 -1%: remaining Apple modem share largely gone, handset units flat, auto (+30-60%) and IoT offset most of it. FY28-30 +3-5%: auto/PC/IoT compounding plus data center contributing modestly (well below the $5B/$15B targets). Fades to 3% vs a 5.8% through-cycle 10y CAGR.
base.margin_rationale: Adj EBITDA recovers from the FY26E ~32.7% trough as AI/data-center opex is absorbed, to 36% -- below the FY24-25 37-38% because the Apple flagship-modem mix leaves and data-center racks carry lower gross margin. QTL keeps its ~70%+ EBT margin throughout.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax ~17-18% in FY27-28 while the 2025 restoration of domestic R&D expensing (Sec. 174 catch-up) shelters cash tax, then a normal ~19% (FDII-benefited) blended cash rate; FY24-25 cash taxes paid $3.3B/$3.1B were ~25% of pretax under capitalised R&D.
base.capex_rationale: Capex ran 4.8% of revenue in 9M FY26 (data-center build, Alphawave); normalises toward the FY24-25 2.7-3.0% fabless level, held slightly above at 3.2%.
base.wc_rationale: Fabless chip seller: receivables + inventory exceed payables, so growth consumes cash (negative capture on the revenue change).

scenario_narratives.base: Apple's in-house modem finishes displacing Qualcomm across the iPhone line by FY27, taking several billion of QCT handset revenue; Android flagship share (Samsung, Xiaomi, Oppo/Vivo) holds against MediaTek, and global smartphone units stay flat. Automotive (Snapdragon Digital Chassis backlog) and IoT/PC compound at double digits, and the AI200/AI250 data-center business ships into HUMAIN but lands at a fraction of management's $5B/$15B targets -- enough, with auto, to replace the Apple hole and return revenue to mid-single-digit growth from FY29. QTL royalties stay stable at ~$5.5-6B. Margins recover from the FY26 investment trough but settle below the FY24-25 level on mix.
scenario_narratives.bull: Data center AI becomes a real third leg: HUMAIN's 200MW plus at least one hyperscaler win take data-center revenue into the mid-single-digit billions by FY29, Alphawave connectivity IP attaches to custom silicon, and the Arm judgment lets Oryon CPUs win share in Windows PCs. Automotive reaches the ~$8B+ pipeline management points to, the handset business benefits from an on-device-AI upgrade cycle, and operating leverage on the now-built opex base lifts adj EBITDA margin back above 38%. Revenue compounds high-single-digit for three years.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Apple loss lands at once while a China-led smartphone downturn (memory-cost inflation, MediaTek and in-house Chinese silicon) shrinks the Android handset pool; the AI200/AI250 racks fail to win beyond HUMAIN against Nvidia, AMD and hyperscaler ASICs, leaving a costly opex build stranded. A renewed antitrust or licensee challenge to 'no license, no chips' trims QTL rates. Revenue falls ~9% over two years and recovers only at GDP-like rates; margins stay near the FY26 trough.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the largest customer is actively leaving and the diversification thesis rests partly on an unproven data-center pivot. Base 50%: auto/IoT growth is visible in reported records and backlog. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs data center, PC share and a handset upgrade cycle to all go right at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: QCOM is valued as a cyclical fabless semiconductor plus a stable licensing annuity on a strict owner-FCF basis: SBC and the cash taxes paid on net-share settlement (~10% of revenue combined) are charged in the flows and the share count held flat. The FY26 trough (revenue -3%, margins compressed by AI/data-center opex) is not carried forward; margins recover toward but not back to the FY24-25 mix. The terminal value is capped at a cyclical 14x (16x bull, 12x bear) rather than a growth-tech 20x. The data-center business is treated as an option realised mainly in the bull case.
key_risks_to_valuation: Apple modem attrition faster or deeper than base (largest historical QCT customer)
AI200/AI250 data-center revenue fails to scale beyond HUMAIN, stranding the opex build
Antitrust/licensee challenge to the QTL royalty model
China smartphone demand and MediaTek/in-house Chinese silicon share gains
SBC + withholding treatment: the street basis (SBC as non-cash) values QCOM materially higher; the house figure depends on charging ~$4.5B/yr of equity comp
Cash tax: OBBBA R&D expensing and FDII changes could keep cash tax below 19% for longer (upside)
